transcript:
Meeting header: 2026-06-10 15:00 UTC | Duration: 45m | Attendees: Ethan (Redwood AE), Maya (Redwood SE), Lucas (Redwood SE), Jordan (Pelican), Anika (Pelican), Dev (Pelican), Rita (Pelican security)

[00:00] Ethan: Hey everyone, thanks for joining. quick agenda — we're gonna walk through the hosted embeddings api then show a hands-on reranker flow in the Console and talk about Optimize suggestions for lowering token cost. Any must-have items before we start?

[00:22] Jordan: Nope, main thing for us is to see end-to-end latency and how rerank improves our product search relevance. we have a set of, uh, messy product titles and synonyms.

[00:34] Anika: Also timeline — we want a pilot next week if this looks good.

[00:40] Ethan: Great, we'll aim for a 1-week pilot kickoff. Maya, you wanna kick off the demo?

[00:45] Maya: Sure. I'll share my screen — okay, can you all see the Console? (pause) Looks like some people joined on mobile, let me know if it's blurry.

[01:10] Maya: First, embeddings. We use a hosted embeddings endpoint — single HTTP request, returns an embedding vector (512 or 1,536 dims depending on model). Example curl in the docs: curl POST /v1/embeddings —data '{"model":"rwd-search-compact","input":"query text"}' The common pitfall is not normalizing the vectors before running nearest neighbors; our SDKs handle that but if you roll your own watch for cosines and L2.

[01:45] Jordan: Quick q: How do you handle deduped docs and updating embeddings when product titles change?

[01:50] Lucas: Two patterns we see: incremental update pipeline that recomputes embeddings on change events, or periodic full re-embed for smaller catalogs. For large catalogs, use our batch embeddings job — it streams to S3 and you can import into your vector DB. We included an example notebook in the shared drive: https://redwood.example.com/pelican/notebooks/embeds-notebook.ipynb (note: link is placeholder).

[02:20] Dev: Does the hosted embeddings persist anywhere on Redwood side? We want to make sure PII isn't stored.

[02:25] Maya: By default, embeddings are ephemeral and we don't retain inputs for hosted customers unless you opt in for retention. For Private and Dedicated we support customer-controlled storage. Rita, does Pelican have data residency or KMS requirements?

[02:38] Rita: We need to see KMS integration and audit logs; SOC2 is required. We'll follow up after you share the security pack.

[02:48] Ethan: We'll share SOC2 evidence and the VPC onboarding doc after the call.

[03:00] Maya: Jumping into the reranker flow. Typical pattern is 2-stage: 1) retrieve top N candidates from vector index, 2) call Redwood's reranker endpoint which scores/reranks the candidates given the query and some context. I'll post the example request in the chat.

[03:22] Maya: Example payload: POST /v1/rerank —data '{"model":"rwd-rerank-v1","query":"small blue lamp","candidates":[{"id":"p123","text":"Blue lamp - compact"}, ...] }' Response includes score and an explanation token, sometimes a highlight. Watch max token limits in the reranker input if you send long product descriptions.

[03:55] Anika: How much improvement do customers typically see? Any numbers?

[04:00] Lucas: It depends. In retail pilots we've seen +6-18% NDCG on average when moving from pure BM25 or first-stage-only vectors to a tuned reranker. Important: quality depends on candidate diversity and the prompt engineering for reranker.

[04:25] Jordan: Latency? Our SLO is 200ms p95 for the full search path. Can Redwood meet that on hosted?

[04:32] Maya: For hosted, typical two-stage (embed retrieval + rerank) p95 can be ~120-300ms depending on candidate size and model. We demonstrated sub-200ms p95 in similar pilots using rwd-search-compact for embed retrieval and rwd-rerank-lite for rerank. We also covered batching and prefix caching that reduce downstream cost and latency.

[05:05] Dev: What's the tradeoff if we increase candidate N from 5 to 20?

[05:10] Maya: More candidates generally increases recall and gives the reranker better choices, but it directly increases rerank latency/cost linearly. A common pattern: retrieve 20, rerank top 5. Another is to do a cheap lightweight rerank model for initial filtering, then a heavier reranker for the final top 3.

[05:35] Jordan: Any built-in metrics in the Console to compare A/B of rerank models?

[05:40] Ethan: Yes, in the Console's Relevance Studio you can upload labeled sets and run model comparisons; we show precision@k, recall, NDCG and you can export traces. Lucas will demo the UI for a sample set now.

[06:00] Lucas: (screen) Here is the Relevance Studio. I loaded a sample dataset of 500 queries and three model variants. You can see delta NDCG and example failures. We also surface token-level cost breakdowns so you can compare cost per query across models.

[06:30] Lucas: Note that our Optimize tab will recommend quantization for reranker model variants when your workload is cost-sensitive. For instance, switching to int8 quant for the reranker often reduces per-call cost by ~30% with a small quality hit. The suggestion engine shows a projected quality/cost curve.

[07:00] Anika: That's useful. For the pilot we want to test both the higher precision and the low-cost path.

[07:08] Maya: We can configure experiment rollouts in the Console: canary 10% traffic to rerank-v2 while continue ramp to 100% if metrics hold. The Console also has automatic fallback rules in case latency spikes.

[07:25] Jordan: How does caching work for repeated queries? We have a lot of repeated queries during site peak.

[07:30] Maya: We support prefix/KV cache when you use our SDK or the hosted runtime. For repeated query prefixes the reranker can short-circuit and return cached top results. Also continuous batching at the runtime layer batches small requests into more efficient GPU workloads; that helps at scale.

[08:00] Anika: Can you demo a live rerank call against our sample dataset?

[08:05] Ethan: Jordan sent a small dataset earlier; Maya, are you able to swap to his notebook?

[08:10] Maya: Yep opening the notebook: https://redwood.example.com/pelican/notebooks/pilot-demo.ipynb - running the test now. (typing) sending 10 queries through the hosted pipeline.

[08:35] Maya: Output's coming back. p95 numbers here look around 180ms with rerank-lite + compact embeddings, payloads ~2-3KB. I'm posting the raw traces to the chat: https://redwood.example.com/pelican/traces/20260610-demo (placeholder).

[08:55] Dev: The traces show spike for one query ~420ms, what's that?

[09:00] Lucas: likely a cold-start on a particular GPU model variant or a batching boundary. Our runtime warmup and continuous batching aim to smooth that; for pilots we recommend a warm-up traffic pattern for 10-15 minutes.

[09:20] Jordan: Ok good. On the API side, what's the rate limit and how do we request higher throughput?

[09:27] Ethan: For hosted we publish default rate limits in the plan; for pilot customers we lift limits for short periods. For production at scale we typically suggest Redwood Dedicated capacity or a hybrid route policy directing heavy reads to Dedicated while keeping control-plane in hosted.

[09:50] Rita: Quick security question: will reranker input include full product descriptions? We need to redact PII and control access to those logs.

[09:58] Maya: You can control logging level. The default is to redact sensitive fields; for debugging, you can enable request logging which is then stored in customer-specific audit logs accessible only via RBAC. We'll include the KMS/HSM integration doc in the security pack.

[10:25] Anika: How do we instrument evaluation? We want to know when rerank actually improves conversion not just NDCG.

[10:32] Lucas: Instrumentation pattern: 1) collect offline labels and use Relevance Studio to tune thresholds, 2) run canary and collect downstream product metrics (CTR, conversion). You can also pipe model outputs into feature flags so front-end can record which path served each user and join with conversion logs.

[11:00] Maya: I'm gonna show the API curl examples and the small SDK snippets now. remember small differences: embedding endpoints have deterministic dimension sizes and rerank expects candidates as an ordered list. I'll paste examples in chat as well.

[11:20] Maya: (reads) curl -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/embeddings -H 'Authorization: Bearer <key>' -d '{"model":"rwd-search-compact","input":"open frame lamp"}' And for rerank: curl -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/rerank -d '{"model":"rwd-rerank-lite","query":"open frame lamp","candidates":[...]}'

[11:50] Jordan: Any doc on how to tune the reranker prompt?

[11:55] Lucas: Yes, we include a playbook with recommended candidate context length, negative sampling, and a set of small test prompts that help calibrate scoring. We'll share the playbook link after the call.

[12:10] Dev: If we want to reduce cost, what's the best first lever?

[12:15] Maya: Start with candidate N and model size. Move from a heavy reranker to a lighter reranker plus a small second-pass only on ambiguous queries. Next lever is quantization (int8). Then batching/continuous batching to improve throughput. Optimize also suggests TTL for cached prefixes if your queries repeat.

[12:45] Anika: Can the Console show token cost trends per route?

[12:50] Ethan: Yes, the Console bills per-token and shows per-route breakdown. We also show token-level hotspots per call so you can see if product descriptions are driving tokens up.

[13:10] Rita: About the pilot: we need a short SOW and assurances for data handling. Are there templates?

[13:18] Ethan: Yes, we'll send a template SOW and a pilot plan. That will include the scope (50k docs, 1-week), success metrics (p95 latency <250ms, +5% NDCG or +X conversion uplift target), and pricing for the pilot.

[13:35] Jordan: One more Q on vector storage: do you recommend a managed vector DB or using Redwood's vector service?

[13:42] Lucas: For most customers we recommend using your existing vector DB if you have one (Faiss, Milvus, Pinecone) and use Redwood for rerank and hosting models. But for speed of onboarding, our hosted vector store option is easiest — it plugs into the Console and we manage scaling. For very large catalogs or constraints on residency, you might host the vector DB in your VPC and call Redwood's rerank from inside VPC.

[14:15] Maya: Ok wrapping — we've got agreed next steps: pricing + SOW, benchmark script + notebook, security pack, and a pilot kickoff next week. Any final Qs?

[14:30] Anika: Nothing else. Thanks, this was super helpful.

[14:35] Ethan: Great. I'll follow up with the links: pricing, pilot SOW, SOC2 + VPC doc, notebook.

[14:45] Meeting end.

Notes on transcript quality: background noise minimal; some words auto-transcribed (e.g., "rwd-rerank-v1" sometimes appears as "red-rerank"), occasional speaker label swaps in the raw export.
